title: Guarding the Heart: The Spring of Life
speaker: Pastor Doug Leaman

outline.title: The Crisis of Modern Confusion
subpoints: The postmodern age is characterized by a lack of objective truth.
Human autonomy and self-invention have replaced divine order.
This chaos is the fruit of the noetic impact of the Fall.

outline.title: The Failure of Unguarded Hearts
subpoints: Secular thinkers like Freud and Marx reduced man to biological or economic forces.
Worshiping the creature rather than the Creator leads to false anthropology.
The human heart is not neutral; it is filled with idolatry when God is rejected.

outline.title: The Foundation of True Wisdom
subpoints: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge.
Man cannot know himself without first knowing God.
True wisdom comes from God's revelation, not human reason alone.

outline.title: The Imperative to Guard the Heart
subpoints: The heart is the source from which the springs of life flow.
Vigilance is required to maintain a heart aligned with God's truth.
Guarding the heart leads to a wise and holy life in God's presence.

summary:
In this sermon, Pastor Doug Leaman addresses the contemporary cultural crisis of confusion and the absence of objective truth, identifying it as the outworking of total depravity and the noetic effects of the Fall. He argues that modern secular frameworks, such as those proposed by Freud and Marx, fail to provide a true anthropology because they are rooted in the worship of the creature rather than the Creator. The human heart, being neither neutral nor empty, inevitably turns to idolatry when it rejects the worship of God, leading to a 'clown world' of absurdity and chaos.

Contrasting this darkness with the light of Scripture, the message emphasizes that true wisdom begins with the fear of the Lord. Citing Proverbs 1:7 and the insights of John Calvin, it is asserted that man cannot truly know himself without first knowing God. The sermon calls for a return to biblical revelation as the sole source of understanding human nature and purpose.

The central exhortation is drawn from Proverbs 4:23, urging believers to guard their hearts with all vigilance, for from them flow the springs of life. By maintaining a heart aligned with God's truth, believers can resist the surrounding confusion and live a life of wisdom and holiness, reflecting the character of Christ, the architect of mankind.
